column1: # Vhost targets the estate pins — `check-edge-vhost-targets.py` holds the running edge
# to this file and fails when a vhost names a target that is not declared here.
# Only vhosts whose target is a *contract* belong here. A normal proxy host points at a
# service that moves with its container and its UI entry is the truth; these exist
# because each one has already gone wrong in a way nothing else noticed. The first two
# front the admin UI through the SSO gateway (`cerulean-npm-sso`), which left the edge's
# network namespace and left both doors proxying into the edge's own loopback; they named
# the container instead of its address on 2026-11-02, which resolves inside NPM's network
# and nowhere else, so the door worked while `check-edge-vhost-targets.py` called it dead.
# The second column is an address, never a name: a name is only resolvable by whoever
# shares that Docker network, and the check runs outside it.
# domain<TAB>host<TAB>port<TAB>note
admin.monarch.innotel.us
column4: Admin UI door on Monarch's name — SSO gateway

column1: proxy.innotel.us
column4: Admin UI door on the proxy's name — SSO gateway

column1: sage.innotel.tech
column4: Sage session site — TLS terminated by the container, proxied by the edge

column1: # `blueprint` moved from i2 to i1 on 2026-10-30 and its vhost kept dialling the *host*
# address it used to publish from (192.168.1.52:8787), so the name answered 502 from a
# container that was running the whole time. The app also bound loopback only, which the
# move made fatal rather than local: it now passes `--host 0.0.0.0` on its own address.
blueprint.innotel.us
column4: DayZero app on blueprint's own address — moved off i2 on 2026-10-30

column1: # `tv` is pinned because its target kept changing under it: the door moved between Jellyfin
# (14016) and the Monarch SSO gateway in front of Sonarr (14002) twice, and the first repair
# was vhost-only while the panel's row still said 14002, so a regeneration put the gate back.
# On 2026-11-11 the owner settled which one it is: `tv.innotel.us` opens **Sonarr**, so the
# pin names Sonarr's gate and a rewrite to Jellyfin fails here instead. Jellyfin's direct
# publish (14016) is still declared under `iptv`, which is where check-media-doors.py now
# watches the TV client, so the watch-door assertion follows the name that still serves it.
tv.innotel.us
column4: Sonarr — the owner's arrangement as of 2026-11-11; Jellyfin's direct door is `iptv`

column1: # `iptv` is the last door a TV or native client can actually finish: no OIDC in front of it,
# just Jellyfin's own accounts on its direct publish. It stopped being a spare on 2026-11-11
# when `tv` was pointed at Sonarr and check-media-doors.py moved its watch assertions here,
# so the timer now depends on this forward. An unpinned vhost can drift the way `tv` did and
# the watch door would go dark silently — which is the failure that check exists to catch.
iptv.innotel.us
column4: Jellyfin direct publish — the watch door the estate checks, so it is pinned too
